title: Bench hiring sprint: skill-decay index + interview rubric
content:
Purpose and context:
- Quick summary: run a 4-week focused hiring sprint to build a 3–4 person cross-functional bench (infra+serving-runtime+platform) we can deploy into high-priority pods. This is NOT a slow role-by-role funnel; it’s a compact experiment to create ready-to-deploy engineers with a shared onboarding micro-curriculum.
- Why now: forecasted Dedicated/private customer ramp in Q2 requires bench capacity that can be slotted into emergency rollouts or short projects without long tailoring (~2–3 week activation).
- Key constraints: hiring budget for bench limited to 3 hires (IC3–IC4 band), interviews must emphasize practical pairing skills and deploy-readiness.

Goals (SMART):
- Deliver 3 hire offers within 28 days with >80% acceptance probability baseline.
- Average candidate score >= 75/100 across rubric.
- Time-to-first-contribution (TFC): <= 21 days from start of onboarding sprint for at least 2 hires.

Candidate profile (target):
- Core skills: Linux systems, container orchestration (k8s), GPU inference basics (memory/latency tradeoffs), Python + one compiled language (Go/Rust/C++).
- Signals we care about: recent hands-on infra work (past 12 months), shipping small performance/ops fixes, comfort with debugging distributed services, strong pairing communication.
- Soft signals: proactive documentation, async communication, eagerness to learn quantization/serving nuances.

Novel metric: Skill-decay Index (SDI) — quick signal to weight recency of practical experience.
- SDI = sum(weighted months since last hands-on task in key areas) normalized to 0–10 where 10=very fresh (worked on relevant infra within past 2 months), 0=stale (>36 months).
- Use SDI as a tie-breaker in the final score and for onboarding track placement (fast-track vs standard).

Process overview (4-week timeline):
- Week 0 (prep): role-blast + targeted outreach, candidate packet prepared (README, pairing repo, small take-home).
- Week 1: resume screen + quick phone call (30m). Short-list 8 candidates.
- Week 2: pairing exercise (remote, 75m) + systems design chalkboard (45m).
- Week 3: hiring manager deep dive + practical take-home follow-up (as-needed). Reference checks.
- Week 4: calibration, offers, negotiate, close. Onboard start date aligned with micro-sprint schedule.

Interview stages and rubric (weights add to 100):
- Stage A: Resume + phone screen (10) — basic fit, logistics, SDI preliminary.
- Stage B: Pairing exercise (40) — live shared-coding/debugging in a small repo that simulates a model-serving bug (focus on observability/tracing and isolation).
  - Criteria within pairing (out of 40):
    - Problem decomposition & hypothesis-driven debugging (12)
    - Use of observability (logs/tracing/metrics) (8)
    - Clean, testable fix or mitigation path (8)
    - Communication & collaboration (6)
    - Speed + pragmatic tradeoffs (6)
- Stage C: Systems design / operational patterns (25) — short diagram + tradeoffs for scaling a model serving endpoint from 100 qps to 10k qps.
  - Criteria (25): architecture coherence (10), failure modes & mitigation (7), cost/latency tradeoffs (5), evolution/rollout strategy (3).
- Stage D: Cultural/async fit & documentation assignment (15) — short async task: write a troubleshooting runbook for an injected failure scenario.
  - Criteria (15): clarity (6), runbook completeness (5), ownerability (4).
- Extra credit: Open-source contributions / infra tool authorship (+5) — used sparingly.

Scoring guidance and thresholds:
- Numeric total 0–100. Passing threshold for hire: >= 75. Reserve list: 65–74. Reject: <65.
- SDI modifier: if SDI >= 8 add +3 points; if SDI <= 3 subtract 3 points. Max cap still 100.
- Example: Candidate scores 72 raw, SDI=9 => final 75 -> hire.

Pairing exercise design notes (practical):
- Repo: small k8s microservice that proxies requests to a toy model. Preseeded with failing cache invalidation and missing metrics. Candidate must use logs, add minimal instrumentation, and implement mitigation (circuit breaker or backpressure).
- Provided artifacts: docker-compose + k8s manifest + a simple flamegraph capture script (optional).
- Deliverable: collaborative stream (we ask interviewer to share screen 50% of time), candidate writes PR or patch, 20–30 min showing reasoning, 10–20 min QA.

Onboarding micro-sprint (week 0..4):
- Onboarding philosophy: "shipable shadowing" — new hire pairs to finish a small end-to-end task that lands in production by day 14.
- Week 0 (pre-start): access + laptop image, pre-read (serving runtime primer), schedule pairing slots.
- Day 1: orientation (console tour, infra diagram, buddy intro), first small ticket: fix a flaky deploy test.
- Days 2–7: focused learning: pairing on live bug, 3 shadowed runbook updates, join oncall rota as observer.
- Days 8–14: own a small feature/fix with a reviewer; ship to staging.
- Days 15–21: production rollout with safety gates; document lessons learned. TFC goal: contribution merged by day 14 for fast-track SDI hires.

Onboarding checklist (compact):
- Accesses: GH org, CI, cloud project, SRE pager, REDWOOD-CONSOLE sandbox.
- Org setup: calendar blocks w/ mentor, weekly syncs, cross-pod welcome.
- Technical prep: run local k8s dev script, baseline perf test, import sample prompt traces.
- Safety: pair on rollback + canary process, stop-the-bleed runbook.

Offer & comp guidance (bench-specific):
- Target band: IC3–IC4. Bench hires get an accelerated review checkpoint at 6 months focused on deployment runway.
- Signing/extras: modest relocation stipend if needed, one-time learning stipend (USD 1,500), 1:1 credits for conferences.
- Acceptance risk mitigations: staggered offers, maintain 2nd reserve candidate, start-date flexibility.

Decision plays and escalation matrix:
- If two candidates within 3 points: prefer higher SDI; if still tied, prefer candidate with documented shipping history in open-source or prior infra oncall.
- For misses (<65): archive with short feedback note, invite to bench-dev cohort if >60 and willing to upskill.
- Escalation: any offer > 10% above band midpoint requires VP People sign-off (JIRA HR-approval flow).

Notes / TODOs / followups:
- TODO (Priya): finalize pairing repo and test harness by Feb 22.
- TODO (Marcus): craft candidate packet + automated calendar invites.
- TODO (Dylan): prepare SDI scoring rubric sheet and automated Slack post for shortlist.
- Risk: competing market for infra-generalists — consider contractor-to-perm pathways if bench hires fail to close.
- Postmortem plan: if sprint fails to deliver 3 hires, run retro with recruitment metrics and adjust channels; keep all candidate packets for bench-dev cohort.

Appendix: quick interviewer cheat-sheet (bullet form):
- Before pairing: skim resume for concrete artifacts, note 2 prompts about recent bug/obs-work.
- In pairing: encourage thinking aloud, ask for hypothesis, keep time checks, balance help vs assessment.
- After interview: fill quick rubric within 24h, add SDI estimate, leave clear go/no-go recommendation.

Slack/confluence links to include in final packet:
- Bench hiring confluence: CONFLUENCE:Bench-hiring-process-2026
- Pairing repo: github.com/redwood/bench-pairing (placeholder)
- Slack channel: #talent-bench

Quick sign-off checklist for launch:
- Pairing repo ready: Y/N
- Interviewers scheduled: Y/N (need 6 interviewers across 3 weeks)
- Candidate packet ready: Y/N
- Budget approved for up to 3 hires + stipends: Y/N

End of doc.

Notes to self: keep doc intentionally lightweight — this is a sprint playbook not a full policy. Expect iterations after first run.
